description: Hello, this is our first time doing the NASA Space App Challenge. We're a team of three, and we're here to win. <3
summary: Forgotten Explorers is an interactive website that brings to life the stories of eight pieces of NASA equipment left across the Moon, Mars, and beyond. Using an interactive map, visitors can explore each location, discover the equipment's purpose, learn its mission history, and understand the discoveries it made possible. Our project aims to make space exploration history engaging and accessible, inspiring younger generations to explore the science behind these forgotten explorers.
details:
How to open the website

The white circle and arrow show where to press to open the website in full screen. After that, press 'Connect to project'. This should then open the website.

How our project works

Forgotten Explorers is an interactive website that allows visitors to explore abandoned and historical NASA equipment across three destinations: the Moon, Mars, and Beyond.

Users can navigate between the three sections and select markers on the interactive map. Each marker opens an information panel containing the equipment's name, mission history, original purpose, achievements, and current status. The website also uses storytelling to make the information more engaging and help visitors understand the experiences and significance of each explorer.

Benefits and intended impact

Our project makes space exploration history easier to understand and more interesting for younger audiences. It highlights that equipment left behind in space still has an important story to tell, including the scientific discoveries, engineering achievements and knowledge gained from each mission.

We hope to encourage curiosity about space, inspire future generations to learn about science and technology, and help people appreciate the lasting contributions of past NASA missions.

Tools and technologies

We developed our website using StackBlitz, React, and TypeScript. We used interactive mapping, clickable markers, website components, and information panels to create an engaging experience.

Creativity and team considerations

Our creative approach combines interactive mapping with storytelling. Instead of presenting equipment as a simple list of historical objects, we allow visitors to explore its location and discover its story themselves.

Our team considered accessibility, ease of navigation, educational value, historical accuracy, and the intended school-aged audience. We also aimed to create a cohesive visual experience that makes exploring space history enjoyable and straightforward.
